# [STORY] As a maintainer, I want routine maintenance tracked with the same audit trail as feature work, so that dependency/toolchain changes stay traceable

## User Story
**As a** maintainer
**I want** dependency bumps, toolchain upgrades, and small chores tracked as real issues
**So that** routine maintenance stays traceable the same way feature work is, instead of living only in commit messages

## Parent Epic
Parent: #76

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given a Dependabot PR bumps a CI action or a frontend package, when it's merged, then the merge commit references a real Housekeeping Task, not a fabricated feature issue
- [x] Given a toolchain upgrade (Gradle, Spring Boot) happens, when it's committed, then it references the Toolchain Upgrades Task
- [x] Given a pure chore (dead file cleanup, doc archiving) happens, when it's committed, then it references the Repo Housekeeping Task

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Notes
- Spotless is configured in `build.gradle` and runs as part of `check` in `backend-ci.yml` (#101).
- OWASP Dependency-Check runs in `backend-ci.yml` (#101, #105, #106); `npm audit` runs in `frontend-ci.yml`.
- SonarQube and the JaCoCo coverage gate are wired (#108). Sonar is gated to `main`-only pushes, because SonarCloud's free tier discards `develop`-branch analysis — a `develop` push skips that step by design.
- "Independent AI code review" is a practice going forward, not applied retroactively to this Story's Sprint 1-6 work.
